title: Council of Europe and Microsoft sign framework cooperation agreement to promote human rights in the age of AI
source_used: National Technology News (relaying the Council of Europe release; coe.int blocked, HTTP 403)
key_facts: The Council of Europe and Microsoft signed a framework agreement (a memorandum of understanding) in Strasbourg.
Signed by Council of Europe secretary general Alain Berset and Microsoft vice chair and president Brad Smith.
Aim: promote human rights, democracy and the rule of law in AI development and use.

Planned cooperation: dialogue via Microsoft's Open Innovation Centre in Strasbourg, sharing AI knowledge and best practice, and projects supporting linguistic and cultural diversity including regional and minority languages.
Builds on Microsoft's support for the Register of Damage for Ukraine, where its AI for Good Lab assesses damage using AI and satellite imagery.
Also strengthens work on cybercrime, including support for the Budapest Convention on Cybercrime.
The two sides will 'explore areas for collaboration'; no funding or binding commitments were reported.
quote_evidence: "Disregard for international law has caused the rupture in the world order," Berset said.
"AI is creating extraordinary opportunities, but its success will ultimately be measured by how well it serves people," said Smith.
Under the agreement, the two organisations will explore areas for collaboration.
why_it_matters_hint: A leading human-rights body formalises ties with a big AI company, but the deal is a framework with no stated binding duties.
event_date: 6 Oct 2026 (release date per Council of Europe listing)
notes: coe.int blocked (403); text read at National Technology News, which relays the Council of Europe release. Signing date taken from the release timestamp.
